text:
maya: Heads up — we need to reconcile the canary handoff behavior with the new telemetry gating for Dedicated and Private clusters. Observability shows subtle oscillation when a canary drains sessions mid-warmup.

dan: Can you sketch the conditions that trigger the handoff? Is this the probe-failure path or plain traffic re-weighting?

maya: Mostly probe-driven. Example: canary hits p50/p95 latencies above threshold while error rate stays low. Current router does immediate soft-evict of new sessions, but KV prefix cache is small so cold requests spike.

simon: Cold-cache spike makes sense. Two tradeoffs: aggressive failover -> lower perceived latency for existing users but higher token cost and possible request throttling; delayed failover -> longer tail for affected users.

priya: Suggest we add a short "graceful quarantine" window (30s) where router routes new sessions to fallback while continuing to probe canary endpoints for recovery. If healthy after window, auto-merge; if not, escalate eviction.

cheng: That aligns with our earlier idea of a lease ledger. But ledger needs a timeline: who owns decision state? Router only, or a central coordinator?

maya: Proposal: keep fast decisions local to the router (sub-second) using cached policy, and persist final handoff verdicts to the coordinator for audit and long-lived rollouts. Coordinator emits bind/unbind commands back to routers.

simon: Sounds reasonable. Local decisions avoid round-trip overhead for transient spikes. We should define a compact decision schema: {signal, window, action, score}.

dan: We also need a jitter strategy and hysteresis to avoid flip-flop. Maybe exponential backoff on re-attaches and an increasing probe threshold if we see repeated short-lived recoveries.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment 3609989900 started for model v2-small in us-west-2.

maya: Good timing — can we add telemetry markers for: probe-latency, kv-hit-rate, session-creation-rate, handoff-reason? Minimal schema so downstream evals can reconstruct decision edges.

priya: +1 to minimal schema. Also include a probe-credit counter that decays over time; helps differentiate transient noise from steady regressions.

cheng: Implementation detail: store verdicts as events in the coordinator timeline: "canary_quarantine_start", "quarantine_extend", "quarantine_finalized". Routers stream events and reconcile on reconnect. That keeps crash recovery simple.

simon: What about A/B with stateful interactions? If variant B is pinned to a tenant, eviction implies migrating session state or failing requests. We need a per-tenant flag to refuse live migration.

dan: For those cases, fallback should be request-level (route to compatible model variant) not session-level. Add a compatibility matrix in the coordinator so routers can map requests without losing affinity where required.

emily: For rollout safety, make the coordinator expose an API to query current global handoff budget for a model (e.g., max_quarantined_percent, emerg_override). That helps SRE dashboards and automated rollbacks.

maya: Next steps: Priya/Cheng prototype the verdict schema and event timeline; Simon/Dan work on router hysteresis/backoff logic; Emily will draft coordinator budget API. We'll sync in next arch sync.

simon: One more: add a cheap synthetic that exercises prefix caching behavior during canary warmup. If synthetic shows cold-cache spike, use a pre-warm step before shifting any real traffic.

priya: Noted. I'll add pre-warm toggle to the canary orchestration flow.

maya: Thanks all. Filing RFC follow-up with action items. :thumbsup:
